findings.title: appStore map invokes import() eagerly, so nothing is actually lazy-loaded
findings.body: Each property is initialized with `import("./app")` evaluated at module-evaluation time, so importing `@calcom/app-store` immediately starts loading every app package (and bundlers will include them all in the graph). The only change versus the previous static imports is that consumers must now `await`; there is no deferral and no bundle-size/cold-start win. To get the intended async behaviour the values must be thunks (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) resolved on demand.

findings.title: Eagerly created import promises can produce unhandled rejections
findings.body: Because all ~28 dynamic import promises are created at module load, a failure in any single app module (missing dependency, throwing top-level code) results in a rejected promise that nobody awaits unless that specific app is used. In Node this surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection and can terminate the process, even for apps the request never touches. Deferring the import until the app is requested avoids this.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in the `calendar` field, breaking external consumers
findings.body: `getCalendar` is now async, so `getCalendarCredentials()[n].calendar` is a `Promise<Calendar | null>` rather than `Calendar | null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated (it awaits `item.calendar`). Any other caller of `getCalendarCredentials` that uses `.calendar` directly (e.g. API/trpc handlers for connected calendars, availability code) will now silently operate on a Promise object, producing runtime errors or truthy-but-useless values. All call sites need auditing/updating.

findings.title: apiDeletes is populated inside an async forEach callback and is never awaited for recurring cancellations
findings.body: In the recurring-booking branch, `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })` returns immediately; the awaits inside resolve after `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` has already run with an empty/partial array. Calendar deletions for remaining recurring instances are therefore unobserved: failures are swallowed as unhandled rejections and the response can be returned before any event is deleted. Use a `for...of` loop with `await`, or push the promises (not awaited results) synchronously.

findings.title: forEach with async callback escapes the surrounding try/catch and is not awaited
findings.body: Changing the callback to `async` means `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` fires off floating promises: the enclosing try/catch can no longer catch errors from `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` (they become unhandled rejections), and the function returns/sends the reschedule email before the calendar/video events are deleted. Replace with `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { await ... }` or `await Promise.all(map(...))`.

findings.title: forEach with async callback escapes the surrounding try/catch and is not awaited
findings.body: Same problem as the vital variant: the async callback passed to `forEach` is not awaited, so errors from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting` bypass the enclosing try/catch (becoming unhandled rejections) and cancellation of the external calendar/video events may not have happened by the time the function returns true and the email is sent.

findings.title: requestReschedule fires un-awaited async forEach for calendar/video deletion
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { await getCalendar(...) ... })` creates floating promises. The mutation continues to send the reschedule email and webhooks and returns to the client while the deleteEvent/deleteMeeting calls may still be pending, and any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection with no logging. Await the deletions (for...of or Promise.all) before proceeding.

findings.title: Commented example path is wrong
findings.body: The placeholder comment reads `// example: import("./example")`, but the example app lives in `_example` (the previous code commented `import * as example from "./_example"`). Anyone uncommenting it will get a module-not-found error.
